paraphrase: Opening salutation: Oṃ, obeisance to the Primal One, set forth by the Vedas; victory to the one known by itself, whose form is the Self.

original.text: ॐ नमोजी आद्या । वेदप्रतिपाद्या । जय जय स्वसंवेद्या । आत्मरूपा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: After the opening, Jñāneśvar pictures Gaṇeśa as the Word itself — the Vedas and śāstras as his limbs — salutes Śāradā, and bows to his guru Nivṛtti, by whose grace alone he is able to speak.
notes: Ovī range approximate.

paraphrase: Jñāneśvar promises to tell the teaching in Marathi so skilfully that his words will win a wager even against nectar, choosing syllables full of rasa.
notes: The famous 'mājhā marāṭhācī bolu kautukeṃ' ovī; number approximate.

paraphrase: Commenting on the Gītā's teaching of seated meditation (BhG 6.10–15), Jñāneśvar describes the 'royal road' (pantharāja) of the Nāth yogīs: through posture and the bodily locks the coiled power (kuṇḍalinī), asleep at the base of the body, wakes, rises through the centres consuming the body's elements, and merges into the supreme at the crown; the yogī's body becomes light and radiant and the sense of a separate self dissolves. Summary only (restricted practice).
notes: Existence and gist of the passage certain; ovī range approximate; no steps recorded.

paraphrase: On the Gītā's promise that women, vaiśyas, śūdras and those of low birth reach the highest by taking refuge in the Lord (BhG 9.32–33), Jñāneśvar says birth and caste count for nothing once one turns to God: as rivers lose their names in the ocean and every kind of wood becomes the same fire, all who come to him become one with him.
notes: Images recalled at chapter level; verify exact ovīs.

paraphrase: Expanding the marks of the devotee dear to Kṛṣṇa (BhG 12.13–20), Jñāneśvar has the Lord say he carries such a devotee on his head and longs to see him: one without hatred, friendly and compassionate to all, the same in honour and dishonour, content, whose mind is given to him.

Jñāneśvar dwells at length on humility, non-violence, patience, straightforwardness and the other qualities the Gītā calls 'knowledge' (BhG 13.7–11), insisting that knowledge is recognised by these qualities in conduct, not by learning.

On the Gītā's word that one who has become Brahman attains supreme devotion (BhG 18.54–55), Jñāneśvar speaks of a 'fourth' devotion beyond that of the afflicted, the seeker and the one who wants gain: the knower's devotion, in which God and devotee are one and worship goes on without the sense of two.
notes: Location of the 'fourth devotion' discussion recalled as ch.18; it may also be developed at ch.7 (BhG 7.16–18). Verify.

paraphrase: Jñāneśvar gives his lineage: Śiva (Ādinātha) taught Matsyendranātha, he Gorakṣanātha; Gorakṣa passed the teaching to Gahinīnātha, who gave it to Nivṛttinātha with the charge to relieve the beings of the Kali age; Nivṛtti gave it to Jñāneśvar.
notes: Content certain; ovī numbers approximate.

paraphrase: The closing prayer (Pasāydān): may the Lord who is the Self of the universe be pleased with this sacrifice of words and grant this gift — that the wicked give up their crookedness and delight in good deeds; that friendship grow among all beings; that the darkness of sin depart and the world see by the sun of its own dharma; that every being obtain what it desires; that the assemblies of devotees shower blessings on the earth; and that the three worlds be happy.

original.text: आतां विश्वात्मकें देवें । येणें वाग्यज्ञें तोषावें । तोषोनि मज द्यावें । पसायदान हें ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

notes: Original gives the first ovī only. Verse numbers as in the Sākhare numbering (verify).

paraphrase: The colophon: the commentary was spoken in Śaka 1212 at Nevāse on the Pravarā, in the reign of the Yādava king Rāmacandra, and written down by Saccidānanda.

location.ref: Eknāth's colophon appended to the Jñāneśvarī

paraphrase: Eknāth's appended statement that in Śaka 1506 (1584) he restored the corrupted text of the Jñāneśvarī to its purity, warning copyists not to add their own verses.
speaker: Eknāth
notes: Wording of the warning recalled loosely.

paraphrase: Jñāneśvar salutes the god and goddess, parents of the world, who are one reality appearing as a pair: the god is the being of the goddess and the goddess the manifestation of the god; in their embrace the world arises and their duality itself is lost.
notes: Chapter-level summary.

paraphrase: Praise of the guru Nivṛtti, whose grace is beyond words and who is the Self shown to itself.

The words existence (sat), consciousness (cit) and bliss (ānanda) do not describe the reality: each only excludes its opposite — non-existence, insentience, sorrow — and when the opposites fall away the words fall with them.
notes: Chapter attribution recalled; verify.

paraphrase: The word (śabda), though it removes ignorance and points to the hidden, cannot make the Self known, for the Self is self-evident and needs no proof; scripture's power ends before it.
Ignorance cannot exist in the self-luminous reality: if it existed it would be known, and what is known is not ignorance; searched for, it vanishes like darkness searched for with a lamp.
Knowledge too, as a state opposed to ignorance, dissolves: where there is no ignorance, 'knower' and 'knowing' have nothing to do, and what remains is neither.

The one reality sports as the world without ceasing to be itself — the seen is the seer's own play; so the realized one's life is a natural devotion in which God worships God and every act is worship without a second.
notes: 'Cidvilāsa' is the later name for this doctrine; the chapter assignment is approximate.

paraphrase: To Cāṅgadev: the Self hidden in the world is like gold hidden in ornaments; knower, knowing and known are one; to write a greeting one must posit a 'you' and an 'I', yet there is nothing apart to address — so this is the Self writing to itself.
Whoever stands but a moment at God's door has won the four liberations; say 'Hari' with your mouth — who can count the merit?

original.text: देवाचिये द्वारीं उभा क्षणभरी । तेणें मुक्ति चारी साधियेल्या ॥ हरि मुखें म्हणा हरि मुखें म्हणा । पुण्याची गणना कोण करी ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Seeing the form with my eyes, O friend, happiness arose: this is the lovely Viṭṭhala, the lovely Mādhava — my heart is fixed on him.

Muktābāī pleads with Jñāneśvar, who has shut himself in his hut after being insulted: the saint bears the world's blows with a cool mind; if the world becomes fire, the saint must become water; one who is a yogī has a pure mind and forgives — open the door, Jñāneśvar.

original.text: tāṭī ughaḍā jñāneśvarā
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

speaker: Muktābāī

paraphrase: We will dance in the joy of kīrtan and light the lamp of knowledge in the world.

original.text: नाचूं कीर्तनाचे रंगीं । ज्ञानदीप लावूं जगीं ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Nāmdev's songs of Jñāneśvar's samādhi at Āḷandī: with Nivṛtti, the saints and Viṭṭhala present, Jñāneśvar enters the chamber, sits in meditation, closes his eyes, and the stone is set in place; Nāmdev grieves as for a mother.

Invited by Jñāneśvar on pilgrimage, Nāmdev asks what holy place could surpass Viṭṭhala's feet at Paṇḍharpūr and goes only with the Lord's leave; the journey shows that the saints' company is itself the tīrtha.
While grinding and pounding grain I will sing of you, O Infinite One.

original.text: दळितां कांडितां । तुज गाईन अनंता ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Janābāī sings that Viṭṭhala himself sits at the grindstone with her, carries water, and combs and washes her hair, since she has no one else.
The sugarcane is crooked, but its juice is not; why be deceived by the outward colour? The river bends, but its water does not; Cokhā is crooked outside, but his devotion is not.

original.text: ऊस डोंगा परि रस नोहे डोंगा । काय भुललासी वरलिया रंगा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Cokhāmeḷā laments that he is kept from the temple and beaten for 'polluting' God, asks Viṭṭhala why he was born low, and yet says the Lord's name is all he needs.
notes: Summary of a group of songs; individual incipits not recalled.

paraphrase: All colours have become one colour; the Lord is dyed in the dye; the distinction of 'I' and 'you' has gone.

original.text: अवघा रंग एक झाला । रंगीं रंगला श्रीरंग ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Soyrābāī asks: the body is called impure, but whose body is pure? Every body is born of the same flesh and blood; the Lord who dwells within is untouched by pollution.
notes: Gist recalled; wording to verify.

paraphrase: Onion, radish and greens — all of it is my mother Viṭhābāī; garlic, chilli and coriander — all have become my Hari.

original.text: कांदा मुळा भाजी । अवघी विठाबाई माझी ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: If God made Sanskrit speech, was the vernacular born of thieves? The Lord is pleased by devotion, not by the language; the Bhāgavata's meaning told in Marathi is as holy as in Sanskrit.

original.text: संस्कृत वाणी देवें केली । प्राकृत काय चोरापासोनि झाली ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

notes: The saying is Eknāth's and is usually cited from the Eknāthī Bhāgavat; exact chapter not recalled.

paraphrase: The avadhūta tells King Yadu of his twenty-four teachers — earth, air, sky, water, fire, moon, sun, pigeon, python, ocean, moth, bee, elephant, honey-gatherer, deer, fish, the courtesan Piṅgalā, osprey, child, maiden, arrow-maker, serpent, spider and wasp — each teaching detachment; Eknāth draws from each a lesson for the devotee.
The best devotee sees the Lord in all beings and all beings in the Lord; Eknāth makes this vision the mark of the true bhāgavata.
In the Kali age the wise worship the Lord by singing his name together; Eknāth teaches that the name alone suffices in Kali, without sacrifice or austerity.

In the bhāruḍ of the scorpion's sting, a man bitten by the scorpion of anger and delusion (tamas) cries out as the venom climbs to his head; the guru's remedy is the sattva quality and the Lord's name.
notes: Allegorical key recalled loosely; verify.

paraphrase: Paṇḍharī on the bank of the Bhīmā is my mother's home: Viṭṭhala is my father, Rakhumāī my mother, Puṇḍalīka my brother, and the saints my kin.

original.text: माझें माहेर पंढरी । आहे भिवरेच्या तीरीं ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Whoever calls the afflicted and the oppressed his own — know him for a sādhu; know that God is there.

original.text: जे का रंजले गांजले । त्यासि म्हणे जो आपुलें ॥ तो चि साधु ओळखावा । देव तेथें चि जाणावा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Trees and creepers are our kin, and the creatures of the forest; the birds sing sweetly to us; solitude is pleasant and there is no fault in it.

original.text: वृक्षवल्ली आम्हां सोयरीं वनचरें । पक्षीही सुस्वरें आळविती ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: We servants of Viṣṇu are softer than wax, yet hard enough to pierce a diamond.

original.text: मऊ मेणाहूनि आम्ही विष्णुदास । कठिण वज्रास भेदूं ऐसे ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Beautiful is that form to meditate on — standing on the brick, hands resting on the hips, the tuḷsī garland at his neck; this form is my delight.

original.text: सुंदर तें ध्यान उभें विटेवरी । कर कटावरी ठेवोनियां ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: We are dwellers of Vaikuṇṭha; we have come for this purpose alone — to live out truly what the sages taught, and to sweep clean the path of the saints.

original.text: आम्ही वैकुंठवासी । आलों याचि कारणासी ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: It is well, God, that you made me a Kuṇbī; otherwise I would have died of pride.

original.text: बरें देवा कुणबी केलों । नाहीं तरि दंभें असतों मेलों ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: In our house the wealth is jewels of words; with weapons of words we strive; words are the life of our life, and this wealth we share among the people.

original.text: आम्हां घरीं धन शब्दांचीं रत्नें । शब्दांचींच शस्त्रें यत्न करूं ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Tukā is smaller than the smallest particle and as vast as the sky.

original.text: अणुरेणुया थोकडा । तुका आकाशाएवढा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Give me only this gift, O God: that I never forget you. I will sing your qualities with love — that is all my wealth; I need neither liberation nor riches — give me always the company of the saints.

original.text: हेंचि दान देगा देवा । तुझा विसर न व्हावा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: The singing of the name is an easy means; it burns away the sins of many births; there is no need to toil or go to the forest — the Lord comes gladly to your house.

original.text: नामसंकीर्तन साधन पैं सोपें । जळतील पापें जन्मांतरींचीं ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Happiness, when you look at it, is the size of a barley grain; sorrow is as big as a mountain.

original.text: सुख पाहतां जवापाडें । दुःख पर्वताएवढें ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: If the life within is not pure, what will soap do? Outward cleansing without inner purity is useless.
We alone know the meaning of the Vedas; the others merely carry their burden on their heads.

original.text: वेदांचा तो अर्थ आम्हांसीच ठावा । येरांनीं वहावा भार माथा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: In the pool of bliss, waves of bliss; bliss is the very body of bliss.

original.text: आनंदाचे डोहीं आनंद तरंग । आनंदचि अंग आनंदाचें ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: We are going to our own village; take our 'Rām Rām' — our farewell.

original.text: आम्ही जातों आपुल्या गांवा । आमुचा राम राम घ्यावा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Tukārām tells how his guru Bābājī came to him in a dream, placed a hand on his head and gave him the mantra 'Rāma Kṛṣṇa Hari', naming the line of Rāghava Caitanya and Keśava Caitanya.
notes: Content recalled; exact abhaṅga and wording to verify.

paraphrase: By the saints' grace the building rose: Jñānadev laid the foundation, his servant Nāmā raised the walls, Eknāth of Janārdana gave the pillar of the Bhāgavat, and Tukā became the pinnacle; sing bhajan at ease — the flag flutters.

Bahiṇābāī's verse autobiography: married young to an older brahmin, she heard Tukārām's abhaṅgas in kīrtan, received his initiation in a dream, bore her husband's jealous anger until he relented, and remembers her previous births leading to this one.
The true brahmin is known by knowledge of Brahman and by conduct — calm, restraint and compassion — not by birth.

At Paiṭhaṇ, when the brahmins scorned the outcast siblings and pointed to a passing buffalo saying a name means nothing, Jñāneśvar laid his hand on the buffalo and it recited the Veda — showing one Self in all.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: Cāṅgadev came riding a tiger with a snake for a whip; the siblings, seated on a wall, made it move to meet him; seeing mastery over the inert surpass his power over beasts, he was humbled and became Muktābāī's disciple.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: At a gathering of saints Gorā tapped each head with his pot-testing stick and declared Nāmdev alone 'unbaked'; Viṭṭhala told Nāmdev he lacked a guru and sent him to Visobā Khecar, who, found resting his feet on a liṅga, bade Nāmdev put them where God was not — and a liṅga rose wherever he set them.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: When Cokhāmeḷā died under a collapsing wall, Nāmdev knew his bones among the dead because they murmured 'Viṭṭhala', and buried them before the Paṇḍharpūr temple.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: Rāmeśvar Bhaṭṭ, holding that a śūdra may not expound the Veda's meaning, ordered Tukārām to sink his notebooks in the Indrāyaṇī; Tukārām sat fasting on the bank for thirteen days, the notebooks rose dry, and Rāmeśvar became his disciple.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: Carrying Gaṅgā water to Rāmeśvaram for the god, Eknāth poured it into the mouth of a dying donkey, saying the Lord of Rāmeśvaram had received it there.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: A man spat on Eknāth each time he came up from his bath in the Godāvarī; Eknāth bathed again without anger, more than a hundred times, until the man fell at his feet.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: Narahari the goldsmith, devoted only to Śiva, blindfolded himself to measure Viṭṭhala's waist, felt the form of Śiva, and on unbinding his eyes saw Viṭṭhala; he understood Hari and Hara to be one.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: The child Nāmdev, sent to offer food at the temple, wept and threatened to die until Viṭṭhala ate from his hand.
notes: Tradition's account as told by Mahīpati.

paraphrase: Kṛṣṇa came to Puṇḍalīka while he was serving his aged parents; unwilling to break off his service, Puṇḍalīka tossed him a brick to stand on until he was free; pleased, the Lord stood there with hands on hips and remains as Viṭṭhala.

There are four eternal and distinct realities: souls (jīva), countless and bound by ignorance; deities (devatā), powerful but bound; the world (prapañca), made of māyā; and Parameśvara, the one Supreme, who alone liberates.
The devatās can give only worldly fruit and are themselves in bondage; whoever seeks liberation must not worship them but take refuge in Parameśvara alone.
The renunciant should not stay long in one place, should live by begging, harm not even the smallest creature, keep no possessions, avoid worldly company and stay absorbed in remembrance of the Lord.
Among those who seek Parameśvara caste does not count; women and people of any birth may take renunciation.
notes: Position well attested for the order; exact sūtra not recalled.

paraphrase: Prince Haripāla of Bharuch fell dead; Cāṅgadeva Rāüḷ, laying down his own body at Dvārakā, entered Haripāla's, who rose and, turning from royal life, wandered away and became Cakradhar.
At Ṛddhipur Cakradhar receives the grace (śakti) of Govindaprabhu, which the Mahānubhāvas read as the passing of the Supreme's power from one incarnation to the next.

Threatened by the Yādava court — by Mahānubhāva account seized and beheaded, yet living — Cakradhar departed northward, charging Nāgadeva with the disciples and assuring them of his continued presence in the teaching.
Cakradhar teaches his disciples in plain Marathi and bids them keep to it.
notes: Commonly reported instruction; locate in the text.

paraphrase: Govindaprabhu behaves like a child or a madman — playing with children, giving and taking things without reason — acts the Mahānubhāvas read as the Supreme's free play (līḷā).
After Cakradhar's departure Nāgadevācārya holds the disciples to wandering, begging and remembrance of the master, and approves the writing down of his life.

The nine forms of devotion expounded one by one — hearing, singing, remembering, serving the feet, worship, bowing, servanthood, friendship and self-offering; self-offering, in which the separate self is surrendered, is the culmination.
The four liberations — dwelling in the Lord's world, nearness, likeness of form and union: the first three perish with the worlds; union (sāyujya) alone lasts.

The marks of the true guru (sadguru): he gives knowledge of the Self, removes doubt, is himself established in the Self and pure in conduct — not those who give mantras for worldly gain, show powers or deal in medicines and magic.
The marks of the true disciple: faith, dispassion, service, discrimination, longing for freedom and obedience to the guru.

The four conditions: the bound (baddha) are sunk in the world; the seeker (mumukṣu) turns from it and longs for freedom; the practitioner (sādhaka) takes up hearing, reflection and devotion under the guru; the accomplished (siddha) abides in the Self, free of doubt, while still acting rightly.
The marks of the fool: ingratitude, pride, sloth, quarrelsomeness, scorn for the good and trust in the wicked, and neglect of both worldly and spiritual duty.
Effort (prayatna) brings success in both the world and the spirit; the lazy lose both; effort is to be joined with devotion to Rāma.
Discrimination of Self and not-Self: the elements and the body are not the Self; beyond them is the formless Brahman; knowing it through the guru, the seeker is free while living.
O good mind, go by the path of devotion; then Śrī Hari is reached of himself. Give up all that the world rightly blames; do with a full heart all that it rightly honours.

original.text: मना सज्जना भक्तिपंथेंचि जावें । तरी श्रीहरी पाविजे तो स्वभावें ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: At dawn let the mind think of Rāma; let speech utter Rāma first of all.

original.text: प्रभातें मनीं राम चिंतीत जावा । पुढें वैखरी राम आधीं वदावा ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition

paraphrase: Who in the world is wholly happy? Inquire, O mind, and search it out yourself; what you did before, you now reap.

original.text: जगीं सर्व सुखी असा कोण आहे । विचारें मना तूंचि शोधूनि पाहे ॥
original.edition: recalled from memory; to be checked against a printed edition
